subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Back pain for 6 days
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 34 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I've been having back pain for about six days now. It started when I was walking, and my back kind of seized up on me. I've been taking ibuprofen and using heat, but it's still pretty stiff. Doctor: Could you please provide your age, gender, and a detailed description of your current symptoms, including the location, intensity, and any associated features of the back pain? Patient: Sure. I'm 34 years old, and I'm a female. The pain is in my lower back, and it feels pretty stiff. It started about six days ago when I was walking, and my back kind of seized up on me. I don't know exactly what caused it, but I've been taking ibuprofen and using heat, but it's still pretty stiff. It's not on one side more than the other, and I haven't had any numbness or tingling in my legs or feet. Doctor: Have you experienced any bowel or bladder changes, such as incontinence or difficulty urinating, since the onset of your back pain? Patient: No, I haven't had any changes with my bowel or bladder function since the pain started. I haven't had any issues with urinating or incontinence. Doctor: Can you describe the seizure-like episode in more detail? Was it a generalized seizure or localized to the back? Did you lose consciousness or experience any other symptoms during the episode? Patient: It wasn't a seizure like you'd think of with epilepsy. It was more like my back just clenched up suddenly while I was walking. I didn't lose consciousness or anything like that. It felt like a spasm, and it happened pretty quickly. I wasn't sure if it was because I was walking a bit faster than usual or maybe because I had been lifting weights earlier that day. Doctor: Could you

Patient: I'm 34 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I've been having back pain for about six days now. It started when I was walking, and my back kind of seized up on me. I've been taking ibuprofen and using heat, but it's still pretty stiff.
Doctor: Could you please provide your age, gender, and a detailed description of your current symptoms, including the location, intensity, and any associated features of the back pain?
Patient: Sure. I'm 34 years old, and I'm a female. The pain is in my lower back, and it feels pretty stiff. It started about six days ago when I was walking, and my back kind of seized up on me. I don't know exactly what caused it, but I've been taking ibuprofen and using heat, but it's still pretty stiff. It's not on one side more than the other, and I haven't had any numbness or tingling in my legs or feet.
Doctor: Have you experienced any bowel or bladder changes, such as incontinence or difficulty urinating, since the onset of your back pain?
Patient: No, I haven't had any changes with my bowel or bladder function since the pain started. I haven't had any issues with urinating or incontinence.
Doctor: Can you describe the seizure-like episode in more detail? Was it a generalized seizure or localized to the back? Did you lose consciousness or experience any other symptoms during the episode?
Patient: It wasn't a seizure like you'd think of with epilepsy. It was more like my back just clenched up suddenly while I was walking. I didn't lose consciousness or anything like that. It felt like a spasm, and it happened pretty quickly. I wasn't sure if it was because I was walking a bit faster than usual or maybe because I had been lifting weights earlier that day.
Doctor: Could you describe any radiation of the back pain, such as to your legs or feet? Have you noticed any specific activities or positions that make the pain worse or better? Have you had any prior episodes of back pain or muscle spasms?
